# dsh-fs-compact

Token-lean filesystem tools for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): `fs_read`, `fs_grep`,
`fs_glob` and `fs_repl

ace` with compact plain-text output, paths relative to
the session cwd, and a read-before-replace sa

h compact plain-text output, paths relative to
the session cwd, and a read-before-replace safeguard.
> Unofficial community plugin. Not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.
## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `fs_read` | UTF-8 text as numbered lines, 800-line default, `offset` to continue; files above 8 MB

are streamed |
| `fs_grep` | Regex search (pure JavaScript, no native binary); `mode` = `files` / `

content` / `count` |
| `fs_glob` | `*`, `**`, `?`, `[a-z]`, `{a,b}` glob; returns cwd-relative paths

|
| `fs_replace` | Global regex replace, validated in two phases, `dryRun` preview |
Design choices:

- plain-text output, no JSON envelope or bookkeeping fields;
- the path is printed once per group, r

en a target was never read first (or only partially read);
- no `.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, `tar

never read first (or only partially read);
- no `.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, `target` traversal.

## Compatibility

- DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.3` (tested on `0.2.1-rc.3`).
- Node.js 20+ for development and tests.
- Pure JavaS
cript; no native binary and no runtime dependencies.
## Security model

- `fs_read`, `fs_grep` and `fs_glob` are read-only. The plugin makes no network
calls and spawns no

processes.
- `fs_replace` follows the host sandbox policy resolved at call time:
- `read-only` rejec

rectory scans skip `.git`, `node_modules` and build output, skip symlinks,
and stop at 50,000 files

/ 256 MB.
- `fs_replace` validates every target (match count, file size, output size and
policy) bef
ore writing anything; an over-limit call changes nothing.
See SECURITY.md for vulnerability reporting.
## Semantics

**Globs.** A pattern is matched against paths relative to the searched `path`.
A pattern without `/`

also matches basenames, so `*.js` stays recursive while
`src/*.js` is a one-level path filter. `inc

lude`, `exclude` and `replace`'s
`glob` all use the same implementation.

**Replacement strings.** `fs_replace` uses `String.replace`, so `$1` (capture
group), `$&` (whole ma

tch), `$<name>` (named group) and `$$` (literal `$`) are
available. Write `$$` when you want a liter

(named group) and `$$` (literal `$`) are
available. Write `$$` when you want a literal dollar sign.

**Limits and failure behavior.** `fs_replace` first plans every file — counts
matches, checks `maxRe

placements`, file size and the sandbox policy — and only
then writes. An over-limit call changes not

hing and says so. Individual write
failures are reported as `skipped` instead of aborting the whole

batch (already
written files are not rolled back).

**Scanning.** Scans stop at 50,000 files or 256 MB and say so. Symlinks are
skipped. Output is cappe

d at 24,000 chars; `fs_grep` reports files skipped as
too large / unreadable / binary.
## Why it is a bundle, not a plain dependency

DSH's plugin list only shows **profile layers**: packages whose `package.json`
has `dsh.bundle.patch

`. A plain dependency still loads if something inserts it,
but the market UI never lists it (the CLI

even warns
`declares no dsh.bundle — installed as a plain dependency, not a profile layer`).
This package therefore ships:

- `package.json` → `dsh.bundle.patch: ./cordis.patch.yml`
- `cordis.patch.yml` → the `insert` entry
that mounts the plugin

On `dsh plugin add`, DSH's reconcile step applies that patch and appends
`dsh-fs-compact` to `dsh.pr

ofile.bundles`, which is what makes it visible as an
installed plugin.
## Registration gotcha

`ctx.tools.register()` requires `output: { schema, render }`. Omitting
`output.schema` throws `TypeE

rror: tool "x" must declare output { schema, render }`,
and if that throw happens inside `ctx.effect

(...)` it is swallowed — the prompt
section still appears, so the plugin *looks* installed while non

e of its tools
exist. The schema must match the value `execute` returns; this plugin returns
`{ text

ls
exist. The schema must match the value `execute` returns; this plugin returns
`{ text: string }`.

Tools are registered under `ctx.inject(['tools'])` only. The sandbox policy is
resolved at call time

, so a missing `sandboxPolicy` service cannot make the
tools silently disappear.
